summary: The Petitioner, Adani Power Ltd (in short, ‘APL’), has filed the present Petition, _(c) Pass such order(s) as this Ld. Commission may deem fit and proper in facts and circumstances of the present case.”_ (a)This Commission has been determining the tariff of the Udupi Power Project (‘the generating station/Project’) of the Petitioner, from time to time [i.e _.,_ (a) provisional tariff or (b) final tariff or (c) revised tariff], in accordance with the applicable Tariff Regulations. Against such tariff orders of this Commission, either of the affected party prefers appeals before the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity (“in short, APTEL”). The decisions in such appeals consequently resulted in the revision of the applicable tariff from time to time. (ii) The tariff billed by APL based on the final tariff order falls short of the revised tariff as determined by this Commission, based on the revisions in tariff _inter alia_ due to decisions of APTEL or the Hon’ble Supreme Court in appeals preferred against either the provisional tariff order or the final tariff order; _“Having regard to the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case, we deem it appropriate to modify the Order to the effect that the Appellant will pay the provisional tariff as decided by the Central Commission in the impugned order with effect from 01.09.2012 to the Respondent no. 2 in respect of Unit Nos. 1 and 2 till the final determination of tariff by the Central Commission for these Units._ _“11. Keeping in view of the balance of interests of both the generator and the distribution licensees, we pass the following interim order subject to outcome of final disposal of the Appeals:_ 4. During the hearing ‘on admission’, the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the present Petition has been filed seeking execution for noncompliance of the tariff orders/judgement of APTEL by the Respondents. The Commission ‘admitted’ the Petition and issued notice to the parties, with directions to complete the pleadings in the matter. In compliance with the Commission's directions, the Respondent, PCKL, has filed its reply affidavit on 31.12.2024, and APL has filed its rejoinder on 20.1.2025. (e) Pursuant to discussions and reconciliation between the parties, the Petitioner has, in its own letter dated 10.6.2023, revised its calculation of carrying cost and alleged interest thereon, and reduced the amounts claimed by it. Therefore, the invoice dated 27.2.2023 no longer holds the field, and no claims can be made on its basis thereof. The above-said letter, which supersedes the invoice dated 27.2.2023, as well as the details of the discussion/ reconciliation between the parties, has been deliberately suppressed by the Petitioner. On the contrary, it has sought prayers for payment as per the invoice dated 27.2.2023, without disclosing that the calculations therein have been modified. The Petitioner has therefore approached this Commission with unclean hands, and the present Petition deserves dismissal on this ground alone. (a) The Petition is maintainable in view of the Commission’s wide statutory, regulatory and inherent power to execute its own orders. Reliance placed on the judgment of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in State of Karnataka v Vishwa Bharathi House Building Cooperative Society (2003) 2 SCC 412, Transmission Corporation of AP Ltd v Rain Calcining Ltd (2019) SCC Online 1537 and Regulation 65 of the CERC (Conduct of Business) Regulations 2023 read with Section 151 of the CPC. (d) Petition No.155/MP/2019 was filed by APL before this Commission seeking adjudication of disputes relating to the payment of certain (i) capacity charges, (ii) energy charges, and (iii) carrying cost for the difference between the provisional, final and revised tariff based on various orders of the Commission and APTEL over-time. 7. During the hearing, the learned counsel for APL made detailed oral submissions and prayed that the Commission may exercise its powers under Section 142 of the Electricity Act, 2003 and issue time-bound directions to the Respondents for the immediate release of the outstanding amounts. The learned Senior Counsel for the Respondent Discoms opposed the submissions of the Petitioner, stating that payments have been duly made by the Respondents, in accordance with the applicable regulations and the directions of this Commission in the order dated 13.1.2023 in Petition No.155/MP/2019. However, the Commission, based on the consent of the parties, reserved its order in the matter, after directing the Respondent Discoms to file the details of the invoices and the payments made thereof to the Petitioner, along with short notes, if required, after serving a copy to the Petitioner, who was permitted to file its response thereafter. Therefore, the Petitioner’s claim is outside the scope of Section 142 of the Act. 10.
